title: Skylight Refuge
type: Natural hideout, civilian shelter and seed sanctuary
dek: An open-skied cavity where Babel’s adventurers and native survivors try to build safety, protect a Tree-associated seed and decide whether to hide or hold ground.

facts.Status: Safer local surroundings; civilian shelter and recovery base; infrastructure incomplete

Skylight Refuge chronicle · geography, survival, recovery and fortification
body:
Skylight Refuge is a natural hideout in Babel-Ashur, marked on the Greyward Littoral map. The adventurers shelter below an open sky, gathering supplies and planning expeditions while dangerous creatures hunt beyond the walls. Native survivors later share the space, and a Tree-associated seed makes its protection a responsibility extending beyond the company.

Wren’s search and the first night

On 30, Month of Hope, Year 2, Wren leads the company away from the exposed beach into narrow canyons. She refuses a light that might draw other creatures and rigs an alarm with string and her tools. They keep moving beyond the first wet, uncomfortable passage until the walls open into a cavity beneath the sky.

Arjahn judges it good shelter against creatures unable to climb or fly. Eugene struggles through the confined approach, then lies beneath the opening where he can breathe and see the stars. Wren and Aravil arrange watches; the company settles down with food and bedrolls. The narrator confirms a safe night. The base’s later name grows from that practical beginning. Follow the shelter within Greyward Littoral →

A wooded cavity beneath the sky

The cavity is described as roughly a hundred feet in radius, with its overhead opening about two hundred and fifty feet above. A narrow canyon permits approximately one person at a time. Water runs through the Refuge, and plants grow within it; later residents describe a heavily wooded cavern with little substantial construction.

The canyon offers a bottleneck for ground approaches, while the skylight admits light, air and possible approaches from above. The high walls conceal the camp from much of the surrounding terrain. They do not establish that it cannot be found. The water’s origin, treatment needs and connections to other caves remain unknown.

Starting from the bare basics

We are starting from the absolute bare-basics from a survival perspective.Aravil

In January 2026, Aravil identifies immediate needs: reconnaissance, hunting, wood for fires, plant fibres for rope and drying racks for hides. A water source and living vegetation do not supply everything needed for a lasting camp.

Obtaining materials means leaving concealment. Hostile creatures make gathering food, hides, wood, stone and metal dangerous. Wren brings useful tool skills; Aerrow gathers and stores materials. By spring, the company seeks larger quantities from contacts elsewhere in Fenumion. Requests for supplies are progress toward fortification, without establishing completed walls or buildings.

The people who fail to return

By 20–26 January, Wren is present as a stone statue. Aerrow grieves over a living person trapped in stone, rather than a memorial to someone dead. She later returns to normal, but Aravil’s absence raises fears of another expedition lost.

At the May briefing, Olokun describes Aravil’s capture and petrification by mechanical creatures serving a subterranean enemy. She has been recovered by then through a plan developed by Elenia. These events happen on expeditions elsewhere; the Refuge is where the missing are discussed, rescues are planned and returned companions rejoin the group.

Paintings, survivors and two hostile powers

Olokun leaves paintings while seeking Babel’s hidden people. A response near the cave entrance depicts a floating island. Visual communication lets the company learn that someone is watching without requiring an exposed meeting. By May, a rescued person believed to be native lies in a coma-like condition inside the Refuge; the person’s name, cause of unconsciousness and eventual recovery remain unknown.

Olokun briefs Scribonia on 31 May. The underground enemy is associated with mechanical constructs, petrification and captive statues. Another power occupies a floating island or castle, with Titans and reported interference with teleportation. Later nicknames—“King of Shadows” and “king of sparkles”—are informal, rather than established formal titles.

Babelomnys is a name in information attributed to the Zarathians. That name alone does not settle its relationship to either ruler. Mya’s later account says an ancient artifact keeps the floating island aloft despite its dead Tree, and that its ruler fears the being below. Her testimony leaves the artifact’s identity and the rulers’ full relationship open.

Reinforcements and return access

Elenia calls on divine and planar magic to bring allies into Babel, including Aerrow when gathering and survival skills are needed. Bringing him leaves her needing rest. Reinforcement is possible, but costs effort and introduces another person to the campaign’s dangers.

By May, suitable tuning forks matter to return journeys. Scribonia worries that leaving without one could prevent his return; Elenia and Eugene are believed to hold appropriate forks. The company’s access depends on those resources and its powerful travellers, rather than a routine road into the Refuge.

A warning and a rescue

Aerrow reports that monsters are taking over the island and drawing closer to the caves. After a difficult argument over ambushes, fires and ecological damage, Olokun leads Elenia, Arjahn, Scribonia and Gartina back toward the caverns. A fresh blood painting depicts people being driven underground. Bloodied cloth leads them onward.

The party fights mechanical creatures and follows genuine cries for help. Beyond a sealed door, an executioner releases toxin among captives. Elenia calls for aid; Mya’s light frees the captives and protects them from the gas and contamination. That protection does not make them safe from every attack. The enemy’s armor ultimately shatters and its form slips away into the walls as mist, so a permanent destruction is not established.

A nomad recognizes Olokun as the painter and entrusts Elenia with a giant golden seed. The nomad calls it one of four and reports that the enemy has destroyed one. The party promises protection; Gartina begins offering food to the starving survivors. Their later presence at the refuge turns a rescue into an ongoing obligation.

Read the full story: The Blood Painting · The Captives and the Seed.

The people around the fire

  • Kvethe — A defender of Babel’s remaining people who balances secrecy, ecological knowledge, and a refusal to abandon her home.
  • Quille — A young survivor carrying the weight of interrupted succession, hunger, and the daily work of keeping her people alive.
  • Omari — A young voice preserving Babel’s stories while carefully distinguishing what the elders taught from what Omari has seen.
  • Kyrin the Lost — A survivor of petrification whose fragmented memories preserve a beautiful land and the pain of its loss.
  • Rhea — A named participant in the survivors’ campfire whose individual history remains largely unrecovered.

At the later campfire Gartina produces a full meal, and roughly a dozen survivors eat together. Kvethe explains why scattered tribes keep their seed locations secret. Quille describes the loss of the elder she was meant to succeed. Omari distinguishes inherited stories from personal experience. Kyrin recalls farms, vineyards and a lost abundance without claiming a complete memory.

Elenia offers a route to another refuge for those who wish to leave. Kvethe supports safety for the children but insists she will defend the land where she was born. Departure, staying, and hiding the seed elsewhere are discussed; this scene does not establish a completed evacuation or a restored tree.

The cost of going on the offensive

Later, Elenia, Scribonia, Eugene and Arjahn plan to collapse and flood the cavern-bearing mountain. Their motives differ: healing the land, breaking an enemy stronghold, vengeance, and fear of what the campaign is doing to them. The storm and earthquakes reshape the mountain, but the full consequences remain obscured by water, smoke and steam. Arjahn carries Eugene to safety as Elenia escapes the rushing water.

The September gathering still takes place in the shelter, with warm honeyed tea and plans for the next danger. The group then investigates the Luminar Spires and western mist. Those scenes show a community continuing its work; they do not establish that every threat has been defeated.

Read the full story: The Mountain Offensive · Flood and Ash.

Hide, hold, or leave

Aerrow treats the camp as a burrow: emerge carefully, gather or strike, then hide again. He fears that noise, traffic and a growing population make discovery more likely. Arjahn argues that the native survivors’ courage gives the company something worth defending. Neither response makes Babel’s dangers disappear.

By 23 July, Arjahn calls the crowded Refuge a cage and speaks of hating it. He also shapes a corner into a personal retreat. Rest and privacy become needs alongside food and protection, as people live with repeated losses and the pressure of confinement.

Elenia blames herself for bringing companions to Babel and considers sending Dale and Saray away after helping reunite them. Olokun challenges that self-blame: people chose to come and fight, and must retain the ability to choose whether to stay. Their exchange does not make every civilian a voluntary combatant, or prove that Elenia caused each death she fears.

A seed that needs defenders

On 15 July, Elenia asks whether the seed should be planted. Scribonia advises waiting until a stronghold can protect it. The proposal makes fortification a custodial responsibility, while leaving the planting site, timing and eventual restoration unsettled.

We have a Seed of the tree. That's one hell of a victory.Arjahn

In September, Mya describes such seeds as “little trees. Shards of Etz Chaim.” Her account gives the seed a wider significance and introduces the Wyrm’s predation on those Shards. It does not establish that this seed is Babel’s lost central Tree, that planting it is safe, or that the Wyrm is identical to Death or either hostile ruler.

An unfinished stronghold

By 30 July, local refugees fill the wooded cave alongside the adventurers, while little substantial infrastructure has been built. Arjahn’s August proposal for a large door aims to make the narrow approach defensible. Elenia hopes for somewhere they can finally keep their people safe. A proposed door is not a completed fortress.

Well it is better than out there.Elenia

The seed and civilians make abandoning the camp harder. A larger population needs more supplies and defenders, but leaves more traces and cannot move as readily as an adventuring party. Aerrow’s fear of discovery and Arjahn’s desire to hold ground become practical questions about protecting others.

The August discussions of storms, floods and earthquakes also expose the danger of the company’s own power. Elenia considers both burying the subterranean enemy and the possibility of destroying homes, animals and civilians through her own hubris. The later mountain assault visibly alters the terrain; the existing account does not confirm the enemy’s permanent death or everyone’s escape.

August · the Refuge holds, with losses

The hunters’ approach forces a divided defense. Olokun, Elenia and Scribonia draw threats away; Arjahn, Eugene and Nymera remain between the other attackers and the civilians. Eugene finds a fighting position away from the refugees, but the defenders are soon spending their reserves to survive.

Eugene’s Wish destroys two attackers and Arjahn revives Nymera after her first death. The diversion returns badly wounded, followed by two beasts. In the renewed fighting Nymera is reduced to ash; Eugene and Scribonia kill the remaining creatures. The narrator confirms that Skylight Refuge is safe, while warning that not everyone is. The ashes are collected for a later attempt to restore her.

This is the immediate history behind the later turn toward the mountain. Defending a shelter has bought survival without removing the enemy stronghold or ending the work of recovery. Follow the defense through its different witnesses →

Read the full story: The Defense of Skylight Refuge.

October · safer shelter, exhausted return

The October quest opens with the narrator describing the Refuge as safer and ordinary fauna returning; deer wander into the healthy ground. This is a change around the shelter, not proof that fortifications have been completed or that Babel’s hostile forces are gone. Wren returns to friends who welcome her, and Ryvyt asks for a briefing before joining the next expedition.

The jungle and coast remain dangerous. After the mist rescue, the company turns back with Scribonia too weak to walk. Nymera carries him, Wren supplies food and Arjahn escorts them, prepared to provide healing when they reach the cave. The final source message records the escort and intended care; it does not yet show Scribonia’s recovery.

The Refuge’s value now includes somewhere to take people after a successful rescue that has still hurt them. Safer surroundings, a wounded company and unfinished defenses can all be true at the same time.

Safety still to be built

Can its open roof be defended? Does the enemy know its location? Will the seed remain here, and could planting it attract greater danger? The Refuge’s water, walls and concealment support survival without resolving those questions.

The company has a shelter, allies and people to protect. Making that shelter durable requires materials, coordination and choices about whose risks the defenders have the right to take.

The work beyond concealment

The Mark of the Wild hunts show how the Refuge’s practical needs draw people outside: Aravil harvests components, Aerrow scouts for materials, and Arjahn repeatedly asks for wood, stone and metal. By June, rescued survivors make gathering and a rear guard parts of the same obligation.

Aerrow’s fatal February outing and Elenia’s later restoration give the shelter another role: a place to carry someone home when a hunt fails. Materials gathered on later journeys help the company’s plans; they do not independently establish completed walls or permanent safety. Read the hunting history →

A welcome argued over, then earned

Adelia visits Nymera by projection before sending Ryvyt through a Gate. Nymera warns about the danger and asks that he see his friends before coming. Once he arrives, Scribonia challenges his readiness; Saray defends him from her own experience of fighting beside him. The disagreement concerns who gets to judge a companion’s worth before that companion has acted.

After the mist expedition, the Refuge becomes a place of water, coffee, rest and difficult conversation. Scribonia recognizes Ryvyt’s help, but the next expedition remains undecided. His wish to gather divine answers and the company’s suggestions for breathing equipment are preparations, rather than completed safeguards or a new guarantee of safety.

Water and coffee after the rescue

Back at the Refuge, Nymera stretches, puts water close to Scribonia and wishes him better before sitting down. Olokun arrives with coffee and asks how he is feeling. Scribonia answers that he is drained beyond what he calculated: his mind is beginning to recover, but his body has suffered most from the reality-altering effort.

Olokun tells him to rest, thanks him for saving their lives and places the cup within reach. Scribonia uses a magical hand to lift it and drink. The shelter gives the company somewhere to tend the person whose spell helped them escape.

Their conversation continues into what caused the fog, where Scribonia offers a suspicion. The coffee, water and report of exhaustion are witnessed here; neither the suspected origin nor a completed recovery is established by his answer.

The request for a divine meeting later brings Scribonia and companions to the gathering at the Tower of Gael. They make their petitions there; the audience and its answers remain unresolved.

The return without Ryvyt

The next departure begins at the Refuge with Ryvyt preparing help and the company deciding how to cross the mist. Its return is abrupt: Scribonia brings himself, Olokun, Alyhotep and Nymera back from the guarded ruins, but Ryvyt is missing. The shelter makes the absence visible because the companions have somewhere to count who came home.

Ryvyt dies in the ruins. A second opening fails to retrieve him. Olokun wants help, Nymera mourns and Alyhotep examines what might have changed the escape. Scribonia questions the wider cost of another return, then leaves through a portal before the dispute is settled. No attack on the Refuge is narrated here, and no new guarantee of its safety follows from the survivors’ arrival.

Read the ambush, retreat and argument →

Calling beyond the walls

On 27, Month of Death, Year 3, Scribonia gathers Olokun and Nymera in the Refuge’s main area. He wants the gods to hear questions on which, he says, his continued participation in the war depends. Nymera wants to speak with Cala; Scribonia warns that he can promise only a call, not an audience. He takes their hands and carries them through reality. Their petitions at the Tower of Gael belong to the next stage of that journey.

Waiting together also makes room for a smaller uncertainty. Scribonia asks whether Olokun and Wren are romantically involved. Olokun describes a close, teasing friendship; Scribonia accepts the explanation and says he misses her. The Refuge holds companions learning how to understand one another as well as planning the next expedition.

Three days later, Nymera sits in a corner and tries to pray as the others have taught her. She asks Cala why she was chosen and hopes that Oya and the company might someday know peace. The scene records the prayer and its need, without supplying an answer.

A body to recover, a shelter still being built

On 2, Month of the Wyrm, Year 3, Olokun searches the increasingly busy shelter for Elenia and finds her turning a stone in a ray of light. He brings news of the fatal return to the mist: Ryvyt is dead, and they could not bring his body. Elenia remembers asking Adelia for help and feels responsible for the companion who answered. She immediately asks whether they can recover him.

Arjahn emerges from the small hovel he has made for himself. He has been working long hours on the concealed door and was not on the expedition. He objects to another entry into the mist, even with mental protection: reaching the entrance safely still consumes strength needed for the fight. Olokun thinks a larger, better-supported company could retrieve Ryvyt. Their disagreement remains unresolved when Arjahn returns to his work. The door is now an active project; its completion and effectiveness have not yet been demonstrated.

Elenia offers relics and the possibility of asking Mya to guide them. Olokun considers breathing equipment and resistance potions; Alyhotep and Nymera discuss protective magic, the order of entry and gathering plants. These are preparations for a future attempt. The conversation does not recover Ryvyt, identify the prisoner whose aura Abyss mentioned, or prove that any proposed defense will withstand the entrance. Nymera’s account carries another part of the aftermath: wanting to stand in front while believing the others are worth more.
